title: The Giant's Small Quilt
synopsis: A mouse offers a little patchwork quilt to a giant, who finds it makes an excellent blanket for one chilly toe.

related_resources.reason: Pretend-play guidance provides the broad context, not a proof that this scenario improves empathy.
Discussion of emerging different perspectives and pretending is background only; no effect of the giant story was tested.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: They both knew the quilt was much too small to cover a giant.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: The scale problem sets up a gentle comic turn without requiring a moral.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: Parent/caregiver guidance supports only broad age-appropriate editorial practices. It does not assess this original story or prove any cognitive, behavioral or sleep outcome.

rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: The characters repurpose the gift rather than rejecting it; this is an original narrative choice.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: Parent/caregiver guidance supports only broad age-appropriate editorial practices. It does not assess this original story or prove any cognitive, behavioral or sleep outcome.

source_note: Original fiction. Parent-facing sources justify only broad shared-reading/play contexts; fictional stars, giants, dragon sneezes, and the narrative outcomes are not findings in cited research. No sleep or developmental gains are claimed.
